claims.text: For \(q=n-r\), \(J_v\subset\Lambda/I_{r,q}\) has Schur basis \(\{\bar s_\lambda:i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq q^r\}\). [source-2@L1365-L1375|claim=formal-document]

Let \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\) satisfy \(1\le t\le r,s\le n\) and \(t>r+s-n\). Put \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), \(q=n-r\), and \[ v^\vee=v_{q,n-s,q-s+t,n}=v_{q,\ q-i+j,\ q-i+1,\ n}. \] Then \(v^\vee\) is bigrassmannian: \(q-i\ge0\) follows from \(t>r+s-n\); hence \(1\le q-i+1\le q\), \(q-i+1\le q-i+j=n-s\), and \[ (q-i+1)-\bigl(q+(n-s)-n\bigr)=t>0. \] Its parameters are \(i^\vee=j,\ j^\vee=i,\ a^\vee=a=\min(q-i,r-j)\), and \(b^\vee=b=\min(i,j)\).

Writing \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\), the integral Schur involution induces \[ \bar\omega:\Lambda/I_{r,q}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda/I_{q,r}, \qquad\bar s_\lambda\mapsto\bar s_{\lambda'}, \] because \(\lambda\subseteq q^r\iff\lambda'\subseteq r^q\). Basiswise, \[ \bar\omega(J_v) =\bigoplus_{j^i\subseteq\nu\subseteq r^q}\mathbb Z\bar s_\nu =J_{v^\vee}. \]

The 2024 theorem assumes precisely a bigrassmannian \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), defines \(i,j,a,b\), works in the integral quotient \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\), and proves minimality of \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 68-110]

claims.text: Applying Theorem 1.2 to \(v^\vee\) gives minimality of \[ \{\bar s_\nu:j^i\subseteq\nu\subseteq(j^i,b^a)\}\subset J_{v^\vee}. \] Pullback under \(\bar\omega^{-1}\) is the minimally generating family \[ \boxed{\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}} \subset J_v, \] since \((j^i,b^a)'=((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\). Thus the transposed family is minimal, including degenerate \(a=0\) cases (with zero-length blocks omitted).
